title: Working out the high B-flat
summary: Roy woodshedded his range on China Boy and the next meeting ended in a standoff with Rex.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: But I figured I did(?). I went home and I said, "Well..." I'm just sitting, like I sit on the side of the bed, and I'm smoking, and I said, "I wonder if he knew that..." He really tore my ass out, really, and I knew what it was. I said, "If he only screamed that note but he didn't play up through it or back down." And I said, now, if I can work on this thing and get so I can play up in B-flat and play down and play back up there again, in other words, make that my natural range, I'll have it.

And when we met again, I had it. Because that's what I did. I had worked it out. A tune they used to play, "China Boy," the middle note was A-flat, and every time it got to that A-flat part, I was on that B-flat over an A, you know. And I played it up there, not just screamed it, you know. So that was my round, right?

The next time we got together, I figured he was going to do the same thing I did, so I'm waiting on him to see what he's gonna come out with, and he's waiting on me -- and neither one of us played shit! Ha-ha...! You know, we're waiting and (?), and when the night was over, neither one of them did nothin'! That was funny, man. Yeah...
